claims.claim: Excavations have found over 700 wells at Mohenjo-daro
claims.quote: With the excavations done so far, over 700 wells are present at Mohenjo-daro, alongside drainage and bathing systems.

claims.claim: The Indus script has not been deciphered
claims.quote: While the script has not been deciphered yet, many of the images on the tablets match another tablet

claims.claim: Mohenjo-daro was built around 2500 BCE
claims.quote: Mohenjo-daro was built around 2500 BC.

claims.claim: The city was laid out on a grid
claims.quote: Mohenjo-daro has a planned layout with rectilinear buildings arranged on a grid plan.

claims.claim: Waste water ran into covered drains lining the major streets
claims.quote: Waste water was channeled to covered drains that lined the major streets.

claims.claim: There was roughly one well for every three houses
claims.quote: the quantity of wells transcribes as one well for every three houses

claims.claim: The well density was unheard of compared to Egypt or Mesopotamia at the time
claims.quote: This number is unheard of when compared to other civilisations at the time, such as Egypt or Mesopotamia

claims.claim: The excavation photograph dates from 1924
claims.quote:
Archive title: File:Mohenja-daro excavations 1924.jpg
Description: Mohenja-daro excavations in 1924
Date: 1924

claims.claim: India retained the Pashupati seal while Pakistan received the Priest-King
claims.quote: Pakistan asked for and received the Priest-king, while India retained the much smaller Dancing Girl, and also the Pashupati seal.

claims.claim: At Partition some 12,000 finds were split between the two countries
claims.quote: Eventually an agreement was reached, whereby the finds, totalling some 12,000 objects (most sherds of pottery), were split equally between the countries

claims.claim: Some necklaces had their beads separated into two piles
claims.quote: in some cases this was taken very literally, with some necklaces and girdles having their beads separated into two piles

claims.claim: The Pashupati seal is catalogued as Indus seal M-304 from Mohenjo-daro
The Dancing Girl is about ten centimetres tall
claims.quote: A bronze statuette dubbed the "Dancing Girl", 10.5 centimetres (4.1 in) high and around 4,000 years old, was found in 'HR area' of Mohenjo-daro in 1926

claims.claim: The Dancing Girl is bronze and dates to around 2500 BCE
claims.quote: Description: Bronze "Dancing Girl," Mohenjo-daro, c. 2500 BC.

claims.claim: Mortimer Wheeler called the Dancing Girl his favourite statuette
claims.quote: In 1973, British archaeologist Mortimer Wheeler described the item as his favourite statuette

claims.claim: The statue showed the civilisation knew metal blending, casting and other sophisticated ore-working methods
claims.quote: first, that they knew metal blending, casting and other sophisticated methods of working with ore

claims.claim: The Dancing Girl photograph is by Gary Todd and released under CC0
claims.quote:
Author: Gary Todd
Licence: CC0

claims.claim: The city's original name is unknown
claims.quote: The city's original name is unknown.

claims.claim: "Mohenjo-daro" is the modern name for the site, interpreted as "Mound of the Dead"
claims.quote: Mohenjo-daro, the modern name for the site, has been interpreted as "Mound of the Dead" in Sindhi.

claims.claim: Iravatham Mahadevan reads a seal as suggesting the name Kukkuṭārma, "city of the cockerel"
claims.quote: Based on his analysis of a Mohenjo-daro seal, Iravatham Mahadevan speculates that the city's ancient name could have been Kukkuṭārma ("the city [-rma] of the cockerel [kukkuta]").

claims.claim: The name is unknown because the script has never been deciphered
claims.quote: The city's original name is unknown.

claims.claim: The lion-fighting seal image is credited to Ernest Mackay, 1935
claims.quote:
Author: Ernest John Henry Mackay (5 July 1880 – 2 October 1943)
Licence: Public domain

claims.claim: The site could disappear by 2030 according to a 2012 warning by Pakistani archaeologists
claims.quote: In 2012, Pakistani archaeologists warned that, without improved conservation measures, the site could disappear by 2030.

claims.claim: Mohenjo-daro was abandoned around 1700 BCE
claims.quote: by c. 1700 BCE had been abandoned, along with other large cities of the Indus Valley Civilisation

claims.claim: Salinity and poor restoration are causing walls to collapse
claims.quote: Currently the site is threatened by groundwater salinity and improper restoration. Many walls have already collapsed, while others are crumbling from the ground up.

claims.claim: Mohenjo-daro is on the lower Indus in what is now Sindh, Pakistan
claims.quote: Mohenjo-daro is located off the right (west) bank of the lower Indus river in Larkana District, Sindh, Pakistan.

claims.claim: At its height perhaps 40,000 people lived there
claims.quote: The Oxford Handbook of Cities in World History offers a "weak" estimate of a peak population of around 40,000.

claims.claim: The ruins were undocumented for around 3,700 years until R. D. Banerji visited in 1919–20
claims.quote: The ruins of the city remained undocumented for around 3,700 years until R. D. Banerji, an officer of the Archaeological Survey of India, visited the site in 1919–1920

claims.claim: Large-scale excavation followed in 1924–25
claims.quote: This led to large-scale excavations of Mohenjo-daro led by Kashinath Dikshit in 1924–1925

claims.claim: The reasons for the abandonment are still argued — repeated flooding, or land worn out by crops, pastures and brick-making
claims.quote: Possehl coined the possibility of constant mini-floods throughout the year, paired with the land being worn out by crops, pastures, and resources for bricks and pottery spelled the downfall of the site.

claims.claim: The Pashupati seal shows a seated cross-legged figure surrounded by animals
claims.quote: A seal discovered at the site bears the image of a seated, cross-legged and possibly ithyphallic figure surrounded by animals.

claims.claim: The three-faced seal image is attributed to Ernest Mackay
